human_summary: On 7 August 2026, two passenger buses collided head-on in the Kashikapan area on the Dhaka–Sylhet highway in Osmaninagar, Sylhet, Bangladesh. A Sylhet-bound Bengal Paribahan bus and a Dhaka-bound Unique Paribahan bus were involved; police and eyewitnesses attribute the collision to the Bengal bus veering into the wrong lane while overtaking a pickup [ev_99685340cfb96e6d, ev_e7e4274f75924b4d]. Reports say the Unique bus fell into a roadside ditch, and the crash was captured on video [ev_c78334d8553e64e3, ev_8675a512af387063]. Casualty counts conflict: Prothom Alo reports eight killed and at least 25 injured [ev_a50c19158fca4347], while The Daily Star reports nine killed and at least 24 injured [ev_f4f6bf3ae3a5ae94]. All reported fatalities were passengers on the Unique bus [ev_c78334d8553e64e3, ev_f4f6bf3ae3a5ae94]. Time reports also vary, with one source citing around 7:00am and another around 7:30am [ev_8675a512af387063, ev_a50c19158fca4347]. The day-level precision is used due to cluster conventions. A survivor, Faruk Miah, was interviewed [ev_851244544886379c]. Two independent news sources, Prothom Alo English and The Daily Star, cover the event. The identities of casualties were not initially known [ev_189d525e6f97c130]. Main unresolved question is the exact death toll, with official confirmation pending.
